## Nonlinearity Notes for 10/29/2026

| Model | Polynomials | Orthogonal Polynomials | Bernstein Polynomials | Linear Splines | Cubic Splines | Restricted Cubic Splines (RCS) | Kernels |
|------|------|------|------|------|------|------|------|
| Basis | $$1, x, x^2, x^3$$; linear, parabolic, exponential | $$1, x^2 \perp x, x^3 \perp x, x$$; linear, parabolic, exponential | $$\binom{d}{k} ( x^k ) (1-x)^{d-k}$$; skewed right | $$(x-c)_+$$; rectified linear unit (ReLU) activation function | $$x, x^2, x^3, (x-c)^3_+$$ | $$w(x-c)^3_+$$ | $$k(x-c)$$; bell curve (normal distribution), skewed right |
| Tail | $$\infty , - \infty$$; unstable | $$\infty , - \infty$$; potential | A    | linear | exponential (fast) | linear | B    |
| Choices | G    | G    | A    | B    | C    | C    | C    |

# Polynomials
```{python}
# from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
# from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
# from sklearn.linear_model import LogisticRegression
# from sklearn.metrics import accuracy_score
from sklearn.preprocessing import PolynomialFeatures
x_values=habitsdf['study_hours_per_day']  # class
y_values=habitsdf['exam_score']

fitfunction = np.poly1d(np.polyfit(x_values, y_values, 3))


# poly_features = PolynomialFeatures(degree=3)  # decide the maximal degree of the polynomial feature: i chose degree 3 because the relationship looked like it could be modeled with an odd function

# x_poly = poly_features.fit_transform(x_values, y_values)  # convert the original feature to polynomial feature: i put in the true values and want the polynomial feature

# check the extened polynomial features of the first data point
print('original feature (true values):', x_values[0])
print('polynomial features:', fitfunction)
```
